M1.1_P0_gpu_lock_lifecycle_atomicity.root_cause: gpu_lock.py ran as a background gateway: the flock lived in the gateway, the server stop lived in the outer shell's EXIT trap; the gateway released the lock when the inner flow returned, before the trap ran. Also: a server that never became healthy was never stopped (no receipt -> stop_server returned 0; the old test masked this with its own kill_all), and no tree/port/GPU release verification existed.
M1.1_P0_gpu_lock_lifecycle_atomicity.fix: scripts/gpu_lifecycle.py: one supervisor process owns the flock fd and performs identity -> idle -> launch (spawn receipt) -> health -> identity (pinned --pid) -> readiness -> command -> drain -> verified stop -> tree termination -> port release -> GPU release, then releases the lock. run_with_server.sh / run_armB_campaign.sh exec into it. gpu_lock.py: BLOCKED marker (refuses later acquisitions until `unblock --yes` with dead processes) and a signal-safe `wait` gateway (forwards the signal, keeps the flock while the child drains).
M1.1_P0_gpu_lock_lifecycle_atomicity.signals: SIGINT/SIGTERM: forwarded to the driver's process group, bounded drain, cleanup, exit 128+sig; a second signal during cleanup is ignored
M1.1_P0_gpu_lock_lifecycle_atomicity.residual: SIGKILL to the supervisor releases the flock early by kernel design; the next session is still refused by the VRAM idle floor while an orphan holds memory, and the spawn/identity receipts remain on disk for `server_identity.py stop`. SIGKILL of a session is covered by the resume audit, not by an in-process cleanup.

M1.2_P1_gpu_probe_hard_timeout.reproduced: RC4.1 probe_device() accepted budget_s but never enforced it: no TimeoutError could be raised, GPU_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT was unreachable (code review; grep shows no raise site)
M1.2_P1_gpu_probe_hard_timeout.fix: probe_isolated(): the fp32/bf16 matmul + SDPA probe runs in a separate child under a real wall-clock deadline; on expiry the child (ours) is SIGTERMed then SIGKILLed, evidence (child end state, reaped, VRAM before/after) is written, device_state=BLOCKED when the device did not recover. A real runtime can no longer take the in-process path.
M1.2_P1_gpu_probe_hard_timeout.cpu_test_mode: CPU_TEST_MODE_AUTHORIZED requires YUE2_ALLOW_CPU=1-I-AM-A-TEST or --allow-cpu, is labeled 'never a GPU PASS' in the receipt, and exit code 0 from it is only ever produced for an explicitly authorized test run; the lifecycle supervisor records it as NOT_APPLICABLE_CPU_TEST_MODE for GPU release
